items.claim: The only cross-seam device the row discloses at its 10:2|10:3 seam — a shared fool-vocabulary root — is absent from the bytes, and the device that does straddle that seam goes unnamed.
items.evidence: The whole-verse splice לֵ֤ב חָכָם֙ לִֽימִינ֔וֹ וְלֵ֥ב כְּסִ֖יל לִשְׂמֹאלֽוֹ re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Eccl.10.2, and the single_saying call is otherwise sound: 10:2 is a closed antithetic couplet and exact content-token overlap with 10:3 is zero. But the rejected alternative rests on a shared fool root that the consonantal text does not carry: 10:2's fool is כְּסִ֖יל and 10:3's is סָכָ֥ל (plus the ketiv/qere pair) — two byte-distinct lexemes with no shared consonant sequence. Skeleton sweep over ch 10: the kesil skeleton occurs in 3 verses (MT 10:2, 10:12, 10:15), the sakhal skeleton in 5 verses (MT 10:1, 10:3, 10:6, 10:13, 10:14), and no ch-10 verse carries both; the 'shared root' exists only in WEB's uniform rendering 'fool', i.e. it is translation-dependent. The byte-true straddle is lev: לֵ֤ב and וְלֵ֥ב at 10:2 against לִבּ֣וֹ at 10:3 are the only lev-token verses in ch 10 (sweep: 2 of 20 verses in MT ch 10; 26 verses book-wide), and neither the rationale nor the rejected alternative names it. Cross-seam disclosure is therefore misattributed rather than made.

items.claim: The MT 10:3 ketiv/qere is correctly spliced and disclosed, but the row calls it mere pointing variation when the two consonantal texts differ, and it names two neighbour-devices the bytes do not carry.
items.evidence: The pair כשהסכל כְּשֶׁסָּכָ֥ל re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Eccl.10.3, and MT 10:3 is one of the 12 ketiv/qere verses in the disclosure inventory (tier-3, single-witness) — the disclosure obligation is met. The characterization is not: the row calls the two forms 'the unpointed and pointed forms' of one word, but the inline ketiv skeleton carries the article he (k-sh-h-s-k-l) and the qere does not (k-sh-s-k-l) — a consonantal difference (definite vs indefinite fool), not a pointing difference, and one that matters before any token slicing in this verse. Two further named devices fail byte check: the rejected alternative's 'shared heart and fool-root vocabulary' is half false — lev is genuinely shared (לֵ֤ב/וְלֵ֥ב at 10:2, לִבּ֣וֹ at 10:3, the only 2 lev-token verses in MT ch 10) but the fool lexemes differ (כְּסִ֖יל at 10:2 vs סָכָ֥ל at 10:3; skeleton sweep: no ch-10 verse carries both); and device_notes cites a 'lo/root repetition with v.2' when the lo token occurs 0 times in MT 10:2 and 0 times in MT 10:3 (byte-checked). The single_saying boundary itself is unaffected — exact content-token overlap 10:2 to 10:3 is zero.

items.claim: The single-verse call is byte-sound: MT 10:4 is one conditional sentence and its seam with 10:5 carries no shared Hebrew lexeme at all.
items.evidence: The closing splice re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Eccl.10.4, and the verse is a single im-protasis, prohibition אַל תַּנַּ֑ח, and ki-motive clause — the row's one-sentence argument holds on the bytes. The seam is stronger than the row claims: exact content-token overlap 10:4 to 10:5 is zero, and WEB's repeated 'ruler' across that seam is a rendering-level link only — 10:4 has הַמּוֹשֵׁל֙, a hapax in Eccl (sweep: 1 verse book-wide), while 10:5 has הַשַּׁלִּֽיט from an unrelated root (sweep: 5 verses book-wide — MT 5:18 = web:Eccl.5.19, MT 6:2, 7:19, 8:8, 10:5). Two caveats folded in, neither touching the boundary: device_notes labels אַל תַּנַּ֑ח a 'second-person imperative', but the bytes carry the prohibitive particle plus a prefix form, not the imperative — and the staged extract has no morphology layer, so form labels must be argued from the pointed bytes rather than imported from the WEB rendering; and the row cites no neighbour ref, so the byte evidence that most supports its own seam is left unstated.

items.claim: The cluster's sole stated cohesion driver — v.6's asyndetic opening read as apposition — is the chapter's default, is equally true of the verse the row excludes, and the two clustered verses share no content token at all.
items.evidence: Both splices (יֵ֣שׁ רָעָ֔ה רָאִ֖יתִי, נִתַּ֣ן הַסֶּ֔כֶל) re-collate at byte tier. The driver does not survive byte re-derivation. Asyndetic verse-opening is not a positive link in this book: 18 of the 20 verses in MT ch 10 open without a coordinating waw (only MT 10:3 and 10:14 do), and 180 of 222 verses book-wide (42 verse-initial waw). MT 10:7 — the verse the rejected alternative excludes — opens asyndetically too (רָאִ֥יתִי), so the criterion does not discriminate the seam it draws. Positively, exact content-token overlap between MT 10:5 and MT 10:6 is zero, while MT 10:5 and MT 10:7 share רָאִ֖יתִי (sweep: 18 verses book-wide carry the raiti/ve-raiti tokens): the one byte-true lexical tie in this stretch runs across 10:6 and pairs the row's opening verse with the excluded one, leaving 10:6 lexically unattached to either neighbour. 'Apposition' also mislabels the bytes — 10:6 is a finite verbal clause with its own subject and predicate, not a nominal in the slot of the noun it is said to appose. Finally the byte-true refrain that does mark this unit's opening, תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ — the only tachat-hashemesh site in ch 10 (sweep: 27 verses book-wide) — sits inside the cited verse but outside the spliced run and is undisclosed.

items.claim: The single-verse call is byte-supported: verse-initial raiti is an attested book-wide observation opener and MT 10:7 shares no content token with either neighbour.
items.evidence: The splice רָאִ֥יתִי plus its continuation re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Eccl.10.7. The row's discriminator is byte-real: the raiti/ve-raiti tokens occur in 18 verses book-wide, 8 of them verse-initially (MT 1:14, 2:13, 3:10, 3:22, 4:4, 4:15, 8:17, 10:7), and MT 10:7 is one of those 8, whereas at MT 10:5 the same token is embedded inside the yesh-clause יֵ֣שׁ רָעָ֔ה רָאִ֖יתִי and is not the verse opener — so the positional contrast the row asserts is attested, not asserted. Isolation is clean: exact content-token overlap 10:6 to 10:7 and 10:7 to 10:8 is zero in both directions. The straddling raiti tie back to 10:5 is disclosed in the row, satisfying cross-seam disclosure. One correction folded in: the row contrasts 10:7 with the preceding pair's 'asyndetic apposition', but 10:7 itself opens asyndetically (18 of 20 ch-10 verses do) — the discriminator that actually works is the verse-initial position of the formula, not the absence of a conjunction.

items.claim: The stated four-fold template holds for the participles but not for the resumptive-pronoun harm-clause the row actually names, and a book-exclusive nachash device straddling this row's closing seam is undisclosed.
items.evidence: Both splices re-collate at byte tier against oshb:Eccl.10.8 and oshb:Eccl.10.9. The participial opening is genuinely 4 of 4 (חֹפֵ֥ר, וּפֹרֵ֥ץ, מַסִּ֣יעַ, בּוֹקֵ֥עַ), so the cluster is not baseless. But the object the row names — 'participle-subject plus a resumptive-pronoun harm-clause' — is 3 of 4, not 4 of 4: בּ֣וֹ יִפּ֑וֹל, יֵעָצֵ֖ב בָּהֶ֑ם and יִסָּ֥כֶן בָּֽם each carry a prepositional resumptive, while the second colon וּפֹרֵ֥ץ גָּדֵ֖ר יִשְּׁכֶ֥נּוּ נָחָֽשׁ carries none — it names an external nominal agent and puts the participle's referent in an objective verb suffix, and it is also the only one of the four cola with a coordinating waw. Under name-the-object-then-count discipline the stated cohesion is overstated by one colon, and 'without a shift in register' is contradicted inside v.8 itself. Undisclosed cross-seam device: נָחָֽשׁ occurs in exactly 2 verses in Eccl — MT 10:8 and MT 10:11 (sweep: 2 verses book-wide) — and both carry a bite-form of one root (יִשְּׁכֶ֥נּוּ at 10:8, יִשֹּׁ֥ךְ at 10:11; a bare n-sh-k skeleton sweep returns 0 verses because the nun assimilates, so the tie escapes naive sweeps). That book-exclusive pair straddles this row's closing seam at 10:9|10:10 and argues continuity against the cut unless disclosed; neither this row nor the row on the far side of the seam names it.

items.claim: The repeated advantage keyword re-derives true and is uniquely adjacent, but the placement claim is not what the bytes show, the semantic bridge is translation-dependent, and the book-exclusive nachash tie back to 10:8 across this row's opening seam is undisclosed.
items.evidence: All three splices re-collate at byte tier, and the MT 10:10 ketiv/qere is disclosed with the inline unpointed ketiv correctly spliced (הכשיר הַכְשֵׁ֖ר) — the K/Q obligation is met. Byte re-derivation of the cohesion claim confirms it: the yitron token occurs in 9 verses book-wide (MT 1:3, 2:11, 2:13, 3:9, 5:8 = web:Eccl.5.9, 5:15 = web:Eccl.5.16, 7:12, 10:10, 10:11), one token each, and MT 10:10-11 is the only consecutive-verse pair among the nine — real, distinctive cohesion, though the two attested spellings differ (וְיִתְר֥וֹן vs יִתְר֔וֹן), which is why exact-token adjacency for 10:10 to 10:11 registers zero and the claim needed spelling-aware re-derivation. Three defects against it. First, neither verse closes on the keyword — MT 10:10 ends חָכְמָֽה and MT 10:11 ends הַלָּשֽׁוֹן — so 'closes with' and 'bracketing both endings' misplace it. Second, the 'skill applied too late' bridge is not in the bytes: בְּלוֹא לָ֑חַשׁ is privative ('without a charm'), and the temporal sense the row leans on comes from the WEB rendering 'before it is charmed'; the sentence carrying that bridge is also broken mid-clause and contains a positional reference to the neighbouring verse rather than a verse anchor. Third, יִשֹּׁ֥ךְ הַנָּחָ֖שׁ בְּלוֹא לָ֑חַשׁ ties 10:11 back to MT 10:8 as the book's only two nachash verses (sweep: 2 verses book-wide), a device straddling this row's opening seam and undisclosed here.

items.claim: The cluster carries the strongest byte cohesion in this stretch — the only exact-token adjacency in MT 10:1-13 plus a pronominal chain with no in-verse antecedent.
items.evidence: Both splices (דִּבְרֵ֥י פִי, דִּבְרֵי פִ֖יהוּ) re-collate at byte tier against their cited refs. The cohesion is the best in the cluster: the divrei token is the only content token shared by any adjacent verse pair from MT 10:1 through MT 10:13 (the next adjacency is yada at 10:14-15), and 10:13 repeats 10:12's construct with a 3ms suffix. The pronominal chaining is independently byte-verifiable: MT 10:13 carries פִ֖יהוּ twice and no nominal person-antecedent anywhere in the verse, so the suffix must reach back to כְּסִ֖יל at the close of 10:12 — cross-verse dependence in the consonantal text, not a shared theme. The row also navigates the header hazard correctly: MT 10:12 is one of the four verse-initial divrei sites but a genitive phrase, not a header (only 1:1 is), and the row treats it as a construct phrase. One under-disclosure folded in, not enough to unseat the row: the davar root does continue across the closing seam into MT 10:14 (דְבָרִ֑ים) alongside the fool-chain (וְהַסָּכָ֖ל), and the rejected alternative denies re-use of the phrase (accurate) without naming the root-level continuation — which is in any case a weaker tie than the phrase-plus-suffix dependence inside the row.
